thread.title: What Reviewers Are Saying About the New Apple MacBook Air

title: What Reviewers Are Saying About the New Apple MacBook Air
text:
What Reviewers Are Saying About the New Apple MacBook Air By Nov. 25, 2018 8:00 Photograph by Timothy A. Clary/AFP/Getty Images Text size
With so much attention devoted to Apple’s iPhones—and, to a lesser degree, iPads —it’s not surprising that its other devices might get lost in the shuffle.
But Apple (AAPL) also recently released updated MacBook Air laptops. There was also a case-only Mini desktop, but the roughly $1,200 (to start) laptops are probably the more familiar product for most. (The Mac line of personal computers represented about 9% of Apple’s sales in its latest fiscal year, a bit more than iPads.)
Barron’s read a range of reviews to get a sense of the response to the new Air.
“Rather than a ground-up revamp, this new model concentrates on refining the elegant, lightweight design that made the MacBook Air so popular in the first place, while also bringing it up-to-date with features such as the Retina display and T2 security chip,” Cliff Joseph wrote for ZDNet . “And while the MacBook Air certainly isn’t cheap it’s not far out of step with the pricing of rival Windows ultraportables.”
• It’s nice to look at—and to hold—right out of the box, CNBC’s Todd Hasleton wrote . Newsletter Sign-up
“The second I opened the MacBook Air box in the office, my colleagues gathered around and attempted to slide it into purses and backpacks,” wrote Hasleton. “They were giddy that it’s lighter than our work-issued laptops and older MacBooks. I love the brushed aluminum metal body, which makes it feel more premium and more rock-solid than other laptops on the market. There’s barely any flexing or bending.”
• What about computing performance? “The new MacBook Air is a tad faster than the still-available previous model,” wrote Dan Ackerman for CNET . “It’s also faster than the current 12-inch MacBook, which is still running 2017 Intel (INTC) chips, but it’s slower than some comparable Windows laptops in its price class and the base 13-inch MacBook Pro.”
“So: Do you get better performance than before? Yes. Should you expect more CPU power from a $1,199 laptop that weighs 2.7 pounds and has some serious fans? Also yes,” Ackerman wrote.
• Dieter Bohn, writing for The Verge , liked almost everything about the screen except the fact that it’s not a touch screen.
“More than any other upgrade on the MacBook Air, this is the one you’re going to love. It’s a Retina display, which, in this case, equates to a resolution of 2560 x 1600 pixels. It’s sharp and beautiful under a glossy pane of glass, with much smaller bezels. Those bezels are not as tiny as what you can get on some Windows laptops, but it’s still a massive improvement over the old Air,” he wrote. “There is one knock on the screen, though: it doesn’t get as bright as I would like.”
• Luke Larsen called the speakers a “strength” in his review for Digital Trends .
“They now face upward, like the MacBook Pro, just as they should be,” he wrote. “More than that, these are the clearest speakers you’ll find on a thin 13-inch laptop. Music sounds rich, as does videos and movies. For intense media experiences we still recommend headphones, but there’s enough oomph to fill a room.”
• Several reviewers discussed the keyboard, including Dana Wollman at Engadget . “This is the third generation of Apple’s so-called butterfly keyboard, which you can also find on the MacBook Pro line,” she wrote. ”This is one area where a reviewer needs time to just live with the device for a while. The day the new Air was unveiled last month, I said I felt wistful for my old Air’s cushier keys. I added that this wasn’t necessarily a keyboard you could learn to love, but it was one you could learn to live with. At this point, though I still make more typos on Apple’s flat keyboard than I’d like, I’ve gotten used to it.”
• The battery life is as advertised, according to Brian Heater at TechCrunch , who said it’s “a pretty sizable bump over the MacBook, owing to the larger footprint on the Air’s 13.3-inch frame (versus the 12-inch MacBook), with a stated ‘up to 12 hours’ on a charge, to the MacBook’s 10.”
“I found that to be pretty on the money, in my own testing. I was able to stream video for just a hair under 12 hours—plenty enough to get you through most flights,” Heater wrote. Recommended Reading
